question: A conducting rod moving in a magnetic field requires mechanical power of $18\text{ W}$ to maintain uniform motion, and this power is converted into electrical power in a circuit. The electrical output is supplied to an AC circuit at $120\text{ V}$ rms with power factor $0.60$. Calculate the rms current in the AC circuit and explain the energy conversion involved.

options.A: The rms current is $0.15\text{ A}$. Mechanical energy is destroyed in the rod and is not converted into electrical energy.
options.B: The rms current is $0.25\text{ A}$. The electrical power is created without mechanical work because the rod moves uniformly.
options.C: The rms current is $0.40\text{ A}$. Mechanical energy is converted directly into heat without any electrical energy appearing in the circuit.
options.D: $I_{\text{rms}}=\dfrac{P}{V_{\text{rms}}\cos\phi}=\dfrac{18}{120\times0.60}=0.25\text{ A}$. The external mechanical power maintains the rod's motion and is converted into electrical power, which is then delivered as average power in the AC circuit.
